future_check: After any shape or color change, require canonical object-count and palette support plus 600/600 strict task-linked matches.
rationale: The previous per-cell color noise turned one geometric blob into many color-aware diagnostic components and taught a distribution unlike every canonical input. Uniform component colors preserve the mask semantics while remaining easy for structural validators to inspect.
summary: Generated objects are uniformly colored, separated 4-connected components because the authoritative rule forms connected components on the nonzero mask.

future_check: Require each profile exactly 40 times per band in the disjoint 200-draw stability census.
rationale: Exact canonical-profile coverage was 0/60 before repair. A deterministic profile schedule gives every band exact support without sacrificing fresh layout, shape, color, or position variation.
summary: Default sample indices cycle through all five canonical height, width, and palette profiles while difficulty changes the keyed layout stream.

future_check: After any schedule change, exhaust all starts for counts 2–5 and require every five-demo window to refute all declared competitors.
rationale: Counts 2–4 admitted named rivals, while all 150 sliding windows at count 5 were identifiable across easy, medium, and hard. The central role makes the target neither a positional nor color extreme, and separate roles force smaller components to have wider or taller boxes.
summary: Every five consecutive samples contain width, height, and central position/color controls; five is the smallest exhaustively supported demonstration count.

future_check: Keep the named largest_bbox_area rival in lesson_identifiable and require 12/12 lessons after any schedule change.
rationale: An early repaired schedule passed six sampled lessons but one of twelve remained compatible with the bounding-box-area rival. The final six-demonstration schedule always includes a smaller, spread-out component whose box is larger than the target box.
summary: Selecting the component with the largest bounding-box area is not equivalent to selecting the component with the most cells.
